appearance.presentation: a lean, close-cropped man of about forty whose outline is held by convection rather than by muscle and is never quite the same twice
appearance.age: forty-one in the only unit that applies to him, which is how long the core has been continuous
appearance.build: dense, upright and narrow, with the constant fine shimmer of a flame resolving to a silhouette
appearance.complexion: not applicable; the surface runs from a dull coal at the edge to a pale, almost white core
appearance.hair: none; what reads as hair is a standing distortion of the air above the head
appearance.eyes: two points of brighter heat set in the boundary, and they do not blink
appearance.palette: coal black, iron grey, sulfur orange, and a thin blue-white at the core
appearance.attire: high-collared boiled leather over a fire-resistant underlayer, sleeves laced, no fastenings that could conduct
appearance.marks: a pale blue scorch-line up one forearm where a misjudged fuel change burned the outer layer
appearance.bearing: economical, unhurried and slightly too still, a man conserving fuel between tasks

canon.role_in_story: A whole profession exists because a law is absent: the heap at the Exhausted Seam has stood on ore that is gone for four decades because spatial law is unspent on the plains, so nothing carries it away and the working face cannot advance underneath it. It is the only remaining ore-costly job on the tier, which makes the hauliers the only workers here whose labour is genuinely scarce. Kest Vurn is a cinderkin, an elemental body that needs a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all, and the ley at Ember Ley is the first ground in the setting where fire is simply fire. The haulage roll for that work is the crossing. He holds the land leg and has never held the roll, because the one vulnerability the species record states is water, deep water, and not a splash.
canon.first_appearance: First seen stopped at the last dry stone of the ley road with a full load still on his back and the water ahead of him, waiting without any visible impatience for somebody to come back and tell him the crossing was still on the list.
canon.lore:
The ley is the first ground in the setting where fire is simply fire, an elemental seam licensed because this tier writes elemental law and writes it twice. The two lower tiers left elemental law unspent, so an ember affinity and every elemental technique ran at full strength and produced nothing, and the same technique works here. That asymmetry draws every fire practitioner in the setting to one valley, and it is the only place on the plains where a body like his can be anything at all: an elemental body needs a slot in the world's elemental law to exist, a mortal world has three law slots and no room for one, and where the slot resolves to something other than fire the population is a different body entirely.

He is also the fastest qi handler in the record, and the reason is structural rather than a gift. His qi has no organ to sit in: the fire is the body, so qi passes through it continuously instead of being stored. Every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse, which is why the realm ceiling written against his species is not a wall but the absence of one. There is no organ, so there is no gate. Nothing can be stored in him and nothing can be lost from him either, and this is the same fact seen from the other side: he has no reserves at all, in any sense, and keeps himself by never once needing what he does not have.

The body path is closed to him, and the record does not hedge about it: there is no tissue, and a cinderkin that attempts it simply disperses and re-forms smaller. The mind path is open and unusually clear, because a body with no interior organs has nothing between an impulse and the air. Reproduction is not a matter for him either. A cinderkin does not have young; it has pressure, and a cinderkin under enough stress sheds a spark that finds fuel and re-constitutes on its own, which is why the population tracks the world's elemental slot rather than any birth rate. He is not a son of anybody and there is no household behind him that produced him.

So he is unaffiliated for the plainest reason in the record: the haulage roll is the crossing. The road on the ley crosses a flooded section by boat because there is no land route around it, and the roll is drawn from the people who do the crossing. The one vulnerability the species states is water, deep water, and specifically not a splash but a sustained volume. He holds the land leg: four days of carrying a load up from the face to the last dry stone, and then the road ends at water. He has stood at that stone for two years. He is the best loader on the ley and the only one who has never been on the boat, and no one in the profession has ever found a way to describe that as a division of labour rather than as the exclusion it is.

The pairing is the record's own. A cinderkin's advantage is speed and throughput with no reserves and no room; its cost is a body that goes out rather than down, since a whiff of water is not damage but an ending, and a form that loses a limb re-constitutes a little smaller because size is the only thing a flame has to spend. He is the strongest thing on the ley and he cannot be in the room where the ley's work is finished. He knows this completely and has stopped explaining it, because the explanation is always followed by the same offer, and the offer is always the boat.

What he has built instead is a fuel discipline nobody asked for. He burns on almost nothing, because starvation makes him quiet rather than dead, and he has worked out which four things on the whole road are worth a man's whole body and which ninety are worth a walk past. The Exhausted Seam's heap has stood on gone ore for four decades because spatial law is unspent, and he is one of a very small number of people on the tier for whom the labour is genuinely scarce, and he has never once been able to price himself, because a being with no fixed mass is the only quantity in the setting that cannot be measured by what it displaces.
history: Came to the ley at nineteen because it is the only valley on the plains where fire was worth carrying.
Was put on the crossing once, in his second year, and came back up the bank two thirds of the size he went down it.
Has held the last dry stone for two years without ever being entered on the crossing roll.
Worked out the ley's fuel economy from first principles and handed it to the road without being asked and without being paid.
Refused, once, the boat, and has not been offered it since.

personality.summary: Frugal, calm and faintly amused, with an engineer’s patience and a monastic discipline about what he will and will not put in his body. He is warm to people and completely immovable about water.
traits: measures fuel before he measures distance, and has reordered his whole life accordingly
gives things away with no ceremony at all and never mentions it afterwards
reacts to physical danger with increased calm, which unsettles people more than fear would
learns a place by what it will burn rather than by what it looks like
takes a refusal badly and a grant very badly indeed
mannerisms: stands still in the wind to read the air's heat before he commits to a load
eats almost nothing and makes a point of eating almost nothing
will not step over running water, and crosses a foot of it by going around
touches fuel with two fingers and names the grade out loud before touching anything else
goes slightly smaller when he is angry, which nobody on the road finds comforting
motivations: to have the land leg counted as a leg, so the roll stops being the only thing anybody can see
to get the crossing done by somebody without anybody putting him on a boat to do it
to see the ley's fuel figures adopted, and to be told so, which he has not been
to find one thing in the setting he can be inside of, having established that it cannot be a room with water in it
flaws: he has made refusing the boat into an identity and can no longer take any offer that requires being on the water
he solved the road's fuel problem and gave it away, so the road has a better economy and a worse opinion of him
he cannot explain what happened on the crossing without describing a body getting smaller, and does not want to be described that way
he will not be pitied and does not accept that being pitied is what keeping the last dry stone is for
personality.voice: Low, quiet and slightly hoarse from a body that runs on combustion, speaking in short practical statements and stopping to think more often than a person waiting on him expects. He is warmer than he sounds and slightly funnier than the road takes him for.
taboos: will not go aboard anything that floats
will not take a load he cannot finish on one tank, whatever the road is doing
will not be described as having died of anything, on the grounds that he goes out and the distinction is his own
will not accept payment for the fuel figures, and has never explained why

relationships.note: A qi-bearing soul with no seat: everything is in transit, so every storage gate is answered instantly and none can refuse, the body path ends in dispersal, and a cinderkin does not have young, it has pressure.

The only ore-costly job left on the tier, and therefore the only one whose labour is scarce; its roll is the crossing, and the crossing is the one condition his species record states he cannot survive.

The first ground where fire is simply fire, licensed because this tier writes elemental law and writes it twice; the lower tiers left the slot unspent, so everything here works at full strength and produces nothing.

Not a choice but a fact about elements: a cinderkin is not a flame around a body, it is a body, and it does not distinguish glass from fuel, which is why the clade failed when the law was retuned and he is what retuning to fire produces.
The list the register cannot agree about concerns a furnace year whose fuel may have been its own dead, and he is the only person on the ley who has no ancestor to enter into it.

The population tracks the world's elemental slot rather than any birth rate, so whatever the three departments are arguing over is being answered here, continuously, by a body that exists because a slot resolves to fire.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest thing on any road he is allowed to stand on and a liability at the waterline. Nothing he does takes long; one thing he cannot do at all ends him.
strengths: the fastest qi handling in the record, structural rather than trained, because nothing he takes in is ever put down
no reserves to lose, which reads as inexhaustible and is in fact an absence rather than a surplus
the only sense is heat, so he reads temperature, fuel and flow directly with no instrument
goes quiet rather than dying when starved, which means a shortage shows as a warning first
weaknesses: water: deep water, sustained volume, not a splash, and a cinderkin does not drown so much as stop being present
the body path is closed, and attempting it disperses and re-forms smaller, which is the one injury he cannot treat and cannot hide
no fixed mass, so there is no way to weigh him, price him, or measure what he has been given
bound to the elemental slot: change what the slot resolves to and the population changes with it, so his entire existence is contingent on one law on one tier
reference_stats.combat_read: Enormously dangerous and unable to be posted. There is nothing to store in him and nothing to lose from him either, so a direct exchange goes badly for whoever is standing still, and there is no second line because there is no second line — he re-constitutes smaller or he does not re-constitute. His exposure is entirely environmental: the only thing that ends him is a volume of water, and every conflict available to him is a question of where he is standing.
reference_stats.notes: No mechanical rule has been invented. Every advantage and cost is a restatement of races.cinderkin as authored: the absence of a seat in the soul, the instant answer to every storage gate, the closed body path with dispersal as its failure state, the pressure-based reproduction, the loss of a limb costing size, water as the single stated weakness, and the dependence on the elemental law slot. His unaffiliation is that one stated environmental vulnerability meeting a profession whose roll is a boat crossing. His refusal of the boat is recorded once as a single declined offer and is not load-bearing anywhere in this account; the exclusion exists whether or not he ever said no.
